newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland invites bids for up to 65 pct of PBK bank.
newsitem.headline: Poland invites bids for up to 65 pct of PBK bank.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry is inviting bids for no less than 10 percent and no more than 65 percent of its commercial Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), the ministry said in a newspaper advertisement on Friday.
The deadline for bids is February 10 and the finance ministry expects to finish negotiations with shortlisted investors at the end of April.

The ministry said on Thursday that after the end of negotiations with an investor or investors it would begin the second stage of the bank's privatisation through a public offering in autumn this year.

Out of the remaining 35 percent of PBK the treasury will offer 15 percent to the bank's employees and 15 percent to the public. It will keep five percent for a programme to compensate former owners for property confiscated under communist rule.
HSBC Investment Services, advising Poland in the privatisation of its PBK, estimates its value at 1.2-1.6 billion zlotys.

The net profit of PBK jumped 78 percent to 215.3 million zlotys in 1996. It expects a pre-tax profit of 420-430 million zlotys in 1997, up from 370.3 million in 1996, which in turn was 46 percent higher than in 1995.
PBK's balance sheet total grew 24 percent in 1996 to 9.8 billion zlotys. Its shareholder equity was 763.8 million zlotys, 40 percent more than in 1995.

PBK is one of the nine commercial banks created on the basis of former central bank branches in 1989 as part of the reform of the Polish banking system. It will be the fifth of the group to be privatised. Of the remaining four Bank Zachodni is slated for sale in 1998 and three will form a banking group with the commercial Pekao SA bank and may also be sold.
